nodes.name: Asked by the portal
nodes.notes: Read-only. Same header auth as the provisioning webhook. The username is supplied by the portal, which derived it from a VERIFIED Dex-backed session - it is never taken from anything a browser sent.

nodes.name: Whose projects?
nodes.notes: Refuses a blank or malformed username. An unfiltered namespace list would return every tenant's.

nodes.name: Projects they own
nodes.notes: THE SELECTOR IS THE OWNERSHIP CHECK. Kubernetes filters server-side, so no per-item decision here can be wrong. Without it this returns every namespace in the cluster.

nodes.name: Their legacy projects
nodes.notes: Namespaces created before 2026-09-08 carry only `tenant`. Reading both is what stops a legacy tenant losing sight of their own project.

nodes.name: Refuse without querying
nodes.notes: Reached when the username is blank or malformed. No Kubernetes call is made at all.
